intro: I'm an automotive restoration technician. I bring worn assemblies back to spec, form and weld metal to fit, and model parts in CAD — printing them when nothing off the shelf will do the job.

disciplines.name: Mechanical Restoration
disciplines.description: Teardown, inspection and rebuild of worn assemblies — measured on the way apart so it goes back together to a spec that holds up in use.

disciplines.name: Fabrication
disciplines.description: Metalwork made to fit: panels formed on the bench, mounts and brackets cut and welded, repair sections let into original structure.

disciplines.name: 3D Modeling
disciplines.description: CAD models of the parts that have to be replaced, adapted or made from nothing — measured first, drawn to fit the car it is going in.

disciplines.name: Additive Manufacturing
disciplines.description: Printed parts, patterns and fixtures — replacements for parts no longer made, and the tooling that makes the rest of the job easier.
